supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded two failed network logons for raul.diaz from 198.51.100.77; both report an incorrect-password substatus.
About 81 seconds after the second failure, the domain controller recorded a successful NTLM network logon for raul.diaz from the same source address.
The successful network logon from that source is inconsistent with the inventory's stated remote-administration practice: no VPN, and remote administration only from WS-SBYRNE-01.

Raul also had a separate interactive logon on WS-RDIAZ-01 earlier in the review window; its logon ID differs from the later network logon, so it does not establish that the network authentication was part of that local session.

known_telemetry_limitations: The domain-controller records identify the source as 198.51.100.77 but do not identify the device or person behind that address. (T271-00015, T271-00016, T271-00018)
The successful logon record does not show what resource was accessed or what actions followed. (T271-00018)
The available records do not establish whether the successful authentication was authorized or whether the password was compromised.
claims_not_established: The identity, location, or ownership of the source represented by 198.51.100.77 is not established by these records. (T271-00015, T271-00016, T271-00018)
The records do not establish what the successful network logon accessed or whether it led to further activity. (T271-00018)
The records do not establish whether raul.diaz or an authorized operator initiated the authentication.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate 198.51.100.77 with network, firewall, DHCP, and endpoint records to identify the originating device and determine whether the address is expected.
Review domain-controller and target-resource logs associated with the successful logon ID 0x149f03dc for accessed services, resources, and subsequent activity.
Confirm with raul.diaz and IT whether this authentication was expected; review relevant account and password-change history.
unrelated_findings: Firefox on WS-RDIAZ-01 accessed Facebook and established a proxy tunnel to slack.com; Slack is not listed among approved services. These observations do not determine whether the alerted authentication was malicious. (T271-00023, T271-00028, T271-00031, T271-00032)
